newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa Airplus ups card profits 18pct.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Airplus ups card profits 18pct.

text.p: Lufthansa Airplus Servicekarten GmbH said it improved net profits 18 percent to 16.6 million marks last year.
The Deutsche Lufthansa AG credit card subsidiary said it increased its trading volume 16 percent to seven billion marks and raised card numbers 25 percent to 231,000.
Lufthansa Airplus joint managing director Peter Metzler told a news conference: "Lufthansa Airplus is now the third-largest credit card system in Germany after Eurocard and Visa."
In 1997, the card company expected to increase volume 10 percent but net profits were likely to stagnate at this year's level, he said.
Metzler said the company improved its share of German air travel credit card reservations to 76 percent last year from 70 percent in 1995.
Lufthansa Airplus achieved an average transaction value of slightly over 500 marks from its 13.8 million annual transactions in 1996, he added.
Joint managing director Anton Lill said the Airplus annual revenue per cardholder of 14,800 marks was considerably higher than the two market leaders with 4,200 marks and 3,300 marks respectively.
The company earned 5.4 million marks of its seven million marks net income from business travel spending while the rest came from other card services, he added.
The overall German business travel market is estimated to be worth up to 70 billion marks, he noted.
Lufthansa Airplus would expand into France, Italy, Spain, Denmark and Sweden this year and thus complete coverage of 80 percent of the European business travel market, he added.
"We want to internationalise with our clients. Our strategy is local sourcing and global consolidation," he said.
This meant companies could use other cards abroad but volumes would be consolidated through the Airplus system. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
